entry.title: II: Persuasion techniques
entry.summary: Book II of Aristotle's Rhetoric covers ethos, pathos, and logos — the three means of persuasion. Out of scope for this showcase.
entry.content:
Book II turns from Book I’s definitions and contexts to the technical core of persuasion: the credibility of the speaker (ethos), the emotional state of the audience (pathos), and the patterns of reasoning an orator relies on (logos). Aristotle works through each mode in turn, including a systematic survey of the emotions and a catalogue of common argument patterns and their pitfalls.

This showcase converts Book I only — Book II’s chapters are out of scope here. This page is a landing only, so the section stays navigable without dangling links.
